Ensuring the safe offloading of captured CO₂ at Aptamus’ T-RICH hub requires addressing not only the technical infrastructure details but also the broader industry uncertainties, such as the lack of global standards for CO₂ purity and best practices in pressure-temperature conditions. Here's how the system responds within this evolving context: 1. Manifold Connection: Ships connect to the T-RICH berth’s loading arm using ISO-standardized flanges. However, current standards do not specify requirements for CO₂ impurities, such as sulfur compounds and residual amines, which could corrode seals or compromise storage integrity. The design would incorporate quick-release couplings with dual-ball valves and emergency shut-off triggers. Yet, the absence of global guidelines for CO₂ composition suggests that emerging Carbon Capture technologies may introduce unregulated contaminants unknown at this time. Accommodating CO from emerging Carbon Capture technologies 2 might introduce necessary modifications to the equipment. 2. Pressure & Temperature Control: While the T-RICH site’s storage tanks and associated equipment will be designed for a pressure range of approximately 15 to 18 bar and a corresponding temperature range of -25°C to -30°C, there is no standardized pressure-temperature regime for maritime CO₂ carriage and offloading. This lack of standardization poses future connectivity uncertainties. Ships employing various capture technologies, such as low-pressure cryogenic or high-pressure amine systems, might deliver CO₂ outside the hub’s compatibility range, requiring expensive retrofits. 3. Transfer Equipment: Cryogenic pumps and insulated hoses are designed and constructed according to industry standards and best practices. However, the absence of standardized carbon capture equipment requirements might introduce mandatory equipment upgrades and changes to maintenance practices due to evolving legislation. 4. Operational Workflow Recommendations: Pre-connection screening of the offloading ship’s CO quality is a critical quality control measure that must 2 be implemented to ensure the integrity and safety of shipments. By rejecting shipments that exceed specified contaminant thresholds, such as more than 100 parts per million (ppm) of water (H₂O) or over 50 ppm of amines, this process helps maintain the purity standards of the received CO . This screening 2 step is particularly important in industries where even small amounts of impurities can significantly impact product quality, process efficiency, or safety.
